title: follow-cam action spotting, data test: the pilot's recipe on 5 training matches instead of 2
written: 2026-11-23, after the pilot's result (pilot_eval.json, gate not met), before any new crop is generated or any model trained
owner request: 2026-11-23: 'Oui, prepare le plan sur 6 matchs' -- does more annotated data give a learning signal? M1 (117092) is left out: its truth boxes do not fit its video's pixels (m1/reading_m1.json), so the virtual camera would aim off; 5 training matches remain
question: with the same model, camera and compute as the pilot, does going from 2 to 5 training matches make shots and tackles detectable?
data: SoccerTrack v2 v1.2 (CC BY 4.0). Training: M3 118575, M4 118576, M5 118577, M6 118578, M8 128058, both halves (10 halves; 136 SHOT, 171 PLAYER SUCCESSFUL TACKLE, vs 59 and 69 in the pilot). Validation loss during training: M2 117093, as in the pilot. Evaluation: M2 117093 and M10 132877, both halves, whole videos (48 SHOT + 8 GOAL, 50 PLAYER SUCCESSFUL TACKLE). M7 / M9 untouched; M1 not used
unchanged from plan.json (sha256 838c947: the virtual camera, the crops (gen_crops.py; the pilot's M2 / M3 / M4 crops reused as they are), the labels, the model and its config, T-DEED commit d953b4d with tdeed_patch.py's four patches, ImageNet weights only (no SoccerNet weights), the evaluation code (evaluate.py's NMS, matching, AP and random baseline)
crop check (before training, no score): for each new half, 12 frames evenly spaced in crops.mp4 on a contact sheet, looked at: a half is kept if players are in view on at least 10 of 12 frames; a dropped half is named in the record and the run goes on without it
schedule (the pilot's, so the comparison: 20 epochs x 100,000 frames, warm-up 2, batch 4 accumulated over 4 steps (-ag 4), Kaggle T4; model kept = last epoch (no selection on M2 or M10). Same compute as the pilot: each training frame is seen ~5.6 times instead of ~14
compute: Kaggle GPU quota is 6 h a week (reset Saturdays 00:00 UTC). Kernel 1, week from 2026-11-28: frames + training, keeps checkpoint_last.pt (~5.9 h). Kernel 2, the next week with quota (2026-12-05 at the latest): scores M2 and M10 with infer.py (~1 h). Disk: frames are ~164 KB each at JPEG quality 92 (~72 GB for 12 halves); extraction checks free space before each half and stops the kernel if under 5 GB; in that case all halves are re-extracted at JPEG quality 80 and the run restarts (a change from the pilot, then stated beside the result)
evaluation: as plan.json, on M2 + M10 pooled (4 halves): per-class event AP with 1-s NMS and 2-s matching, random AP = mean of 20 uniform-random draws (95th percentile reported); shots (SHOT + GOAL) precision at recall 0.60 and 0.80. Also on M2 alone, beside the pilot's numbers (same schedule, same validation match)

decision (fixed now, on M2 + M10).A, learning signal: SHOT AP >= 5 x random AND PLAYER SUCCESSFUL TACKLE AP >= 5 x random -> more annotated matches are the lever: next step is club footage with consent, shots and tackles annotated by the owner
decision (fixed now, on M2 + M10).B, trend: not A, but SHOT AP >= 2 x random AND PLAYER SUCCESSFUL TACKLE AP >= 2 x random -> data helps, 5 matches are not enough; the owner decides whether to look for club footage
decision (fixed now, on M2 + M10).C, no signal: otherwise -> at this scale, more annotated matches do not give a signal from ImageNet weights; annotating more matches is not supported by this test

reported, not deciding: M2-alone APs against the pilot's; mean AP over the 12 classes; shots precision at recall 0.60 / 0.80 against the v4 trajectory spotter's 0.212 / 0.095 (other unit); whether the validation loss still falls after epoch 2
caveats (stated now): the 5 matches share SoccerTrack v2's venue and camera, so a gain may not transfer to Veo footage; ~50 shots and ~50 tackles in evaluation, still noisy; the camera follows the players' median, wider than Veo's (0.35 of the panorama), with no detail finer than the panorama; the 2-match point is the pilot, trained once (no repeat to measure seed noise)
